intent.raw_query: Swiss Alps ski holiday family, $7000, 7 days, February 2026

experiences.name: Skiing at Jungfrau Ski Region
experiences.description: Experience world-class skiing across 213km of groomed pistes suitable for all skill levels. Families can enjoy beginner slopes at Grindelwald while advanced skiers tackle challenging runs from Kleine Scheidegg. Ski school lessons are available for children and adults, making it perfect for family groups of mixed abilities.

experiences.name: Glacier Snow Tubing and Sledding at Männlichen
experiences.description: A thrilling family-friendly winter activity where participants ride inflatable tubes and traditional wooden sleds down groomed snow runs. The Männlichen plateau offers stunning panoramic Alpine views while kids and adults alike enjoy safe, guided snow fun. Equipment rental and lift access are included in the package.

experiences.name: Jungfraujoch Top of Europe Train Excursion
experiences.description: Ride the iconic cogwheel railway to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters, the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace carved inside the glacier, walk on the eternal snow plateau, and enjoy breathtaking views of the Aletsch Glacier. A truly unforgettable cultural and natural experience for the whole family.

experiences.name: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner Experience
experiences.description: Gather around a traditional Swiss fondue pot in a cozy mountain chalet restaurant. Enjoy classic cheese fondue with local Gruyère and Emmental, paired with crusty bread, charcuterie, and warm Glühwein for adults and hot chocolate for children. This authentic cultural dining experience captures the heart of Swiss Alpine hospitality.

experiences.name: Cross-Country Skiing and Snowshoeing at Lenk-Simmental
experiences.description: Explore 80km of groomed cross-country ski trails and scenic snowshoe paths through pristine Alpine forests and meadows. Guided family snowshoe tours introduce children to winter wilderness in a safe and engaging way. The area is less crowded than major resorts, offering a peaceful and immersive winter nature experience at a family-friendly pace.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Swiss Alps, Switzerland
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Zurich Airport at 13:00. Take the train from Zurich HB to Grindelwald via Interlaken Ost (approx. 2.5–3 hrs, use Swiss Travel Pass or buy a saver ticket in advance for budget savings). Check in to your boutique stay in Grindelwald-Wengen. Walk around the charming village center, get oriented, and pick up a local trail/ski map from the tourist office.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the main street of Grindelwald to enjoy the stunning Eiger North Face views at dusk. Visit a local Migros or Coop supermarket to stock up on breakfast items and snacks to keep daily food costs low.

meals.breakfast: Meal on the plane or grab a snack at Zurich Airport (budget CHF 5–10)
meals.lunch: Grab a sandwich or pretzel at the train station bakery en route (budget CHF 8–12)
meals.dinner: Self-catered dinner from Coop/Migros — pasta, bread, cheese, and Swiss chocolate (budget CHF 10–15 per person)

day_by_day.notes: Purchase a Jungfrau Travel Pass or Grindelwald ski region pass upon arrival if planning multiple ski days — multi-day passes offer significant savings. Swiss Travel Pass covers most train legs from the airport to Interlaken.

day_by_day.morning: First ski day! Head to the Grindelwald First ski area (accessible via gondola from the village center). Beginners and families can enjoy the wide, groomed blue and red runs. Rent ski equipment from a local shop like Buri Sport or Michi's Rental for competitive rates (book online in advance for discounts). Hit the slopes early to avoid crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing on the First ski area. Families can enjoy the 'First Flieger' zip-line experience (additional cost ~CHF 29/adult) or stick to the ski runs for budget-friendliness. Take a break at a mid-mountain self-service restaurant and bring your own packed lunch to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village by 16:30. Warm up with a hot chocolate at a cozy café. Visit the Grindelwald Sports Center ice rink for an affordable family evening activity (entry ~CHF 8–12/person including skate rental).

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — muesli, yogurt, fruit, and bread bought from Coop (budget CHF 3–5/person)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch brought from accommodation — sandwiches, fruit, energy bars (budget CHF 0–5/person)
meals.dinner: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald — affordable Swiss classics like rösti and sausages (budget CHF 18–25/person)

day_by_day.notes: Ski rental for a family of 4 can cost CHF 40–60/person per day. Booking in advance online (e.g., Intersport or local shops) can save up to 20%. Dress in warm layers and apply sunscreen — alpine sun is intense even in winter.

day_by_day.morning: Take the scenic Wengernalp Railway from Grindelwald to Wengen (approx. 40 min, covered by Jungfrau Travel Pass). Wengen is a car-free village with breathtaking Jungfrau views. Explore the village on foot and enjoy the peaceful alpine atmosphere. Families can try the beginner ski slopes right in Wengen village.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski the Wengen-Männlichen ski area. Take the Männlichen gondola up and enjoy intermediate runs with panoramic views of the Eiger, Mönch, and Jungfrau. The 'Royal Walk' ridge trail (if snow conditions allow a short walk) offers incredible photo opportunities at no extra cost.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Grindelwald by train. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a family-friendly fondue night — either at your accommodation if it has a kitchen, or at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation (budget CHF 3–5/person)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the mountain or grab a cheap soup at a mountain hut self-service counter (budget CHF 5–10/person)
meals.dinner: Café 3692 or Restaurant Alpenhof in Wengen before returning — try a shared cheese fondue (budget CHF 22–30/person)

day_by_day.notes: The Wengernalp Railway is one of the most scenic mountain railways in the world. The Jungfrau Travel Pass covers this route, making it very cost-effective. Wengen is car-free so all movement is on foot or by train — great for families with children.

day_by_day.morning: Rest day from skiing — take a budget-friendly guided snowshoe walk around Grindelwald. Rent snowshoes locally (~CHF 15–20/day) and follow the free marked snowshoe trail around the Grindelwald valley floor with stunning views of the Wetterhorn and Eiger. This is a perfect low-cost family activity.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Grindelwald Glacier Gorge (Gletscherschlucht) if open in February — entry is approximately CHF 7/adult and CHF 4/child, making it an affordable family attraction. The frozen gorge is a magical winter experience. Alternatively, visit the free Grindelwald Museum to learn about local history and alpine culture.
day_by_day.evening: Head to the village square for a relaxed evening. Try the local sledging/tobogganing run near Grindelwald First (sled rental ~CHF 10). This is a hugely popular and affordable family winter activity.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation (budget CHF 3–5/person)
meals.lunch: Grab a bratwurst and bread roll from a village kiosk or bakery (budget CHF 8–12/person)
meals.dinner: Self-catered hearty meal at accommodation — Swiss-style potato soup, bread, and cheese (budget CHF 8–12/person)

day_by_day.notes: Snowshoe trails are clearly marked and free to use once you have rented the snowshoes. The glacier gorge is a unique geological experience and highly recommended for children. Check opening hours in advance as winter schedules may vary.

day_by_day.morning: Splurge day (relatively) — take the Jungfraujoch excursion, the 'Top of Europe' at 3,454m. Depart early from Grindelwald station (first train ~08:00) to beat crowds. The Jungfraujoch ticket is expensive (~CHF 145–160/adult full price) but with the Jungfrau Travel Pass, you get a significant discount (up to 25–50% off depending on pass type). Book tickets in advance online for the best price.
day_by_day.afternoon: At Jungfraujoch: explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory viewing platform, and Snow Fun Park (included in ticket). Enjoy the surreal snow-and-glacier landscape. Take family photos at the iconic summit. Return to Grindelwald by mid-afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Celebrate the Jungfraujoch experience with a special dinner out — treat the family to a sit-down meal at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before departure — bread, jam, and hot drinks (budget CHF 3–5/person)
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch to eat at the top — the Jungfraujoch restaurants are very expensive. A packed sandwich saves CHF 20–30/person
meals.dinner: Restaurant Pizzeria Grindelwald — affordable pizzas and pasta in a relaxed family-friendly setting (budget CHF 20–28/person)

day_by_day.notes: The Jungfraujoch is the single biggest expense of the trip but is unmissable. Book the first train of the day (Sparticket/Good Morning Ticket) which is significantly cheaper (~CHF 99–115/adult). The Jungfrau Travel Pass provides the best value for families doing multiple excursions. Dress in extra warm layers — temperatures at the top can be -15°C or colder with wind chill.

day_by_day.morning: Final ski day — head to the Kleine Scheidegg area, accessible by train. This is the heart of the Jungfrau ski region with runs connecting Grindelwald, Wengen, and Kleine Scheidegg. Enjoy the wide variety of red and blue runs. Kleine Scheidegg has some of the best views of the Eiger North Face in the entire region.
day_by_day.afternoon: Try the famous Grindelwald–Grund sledge run (one of the longest natural sledge runs in the region at ~15km). Sled rental is affordable (~CHF 10–15) and this is a thrilling family activity. Alternatively, spend the afternoon on easier ski runs with the kids.
day_by_day.evening: Last evening in Grindelwald — pack bags for departure tomorrow. Enjoy a farewell walk through the village to soak in the alpine atmosphere one last time. Visit the local Coop to use up any remaining Swiss Francs on Swiss chocolate, cheese, and other affordable souvenirs.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation (budget CHF 3–5/person)
meals.lunch: Mountain hut lunch — try Bergrestaurant Kleine Scheidegg for a simple soup and bread (budget CHF 12–18/person)
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at Restaurant Alte Post Grindelwald — traditional Swiss raclette or rösti (budget CHF 22–30/person)

day_by_day.notes: Saturday can be busier on the slopes as weekend visitors arrive. Hit the lifts early (before 09:00) to get the best snow and shortest queues. The sledge run from Grindelwald First to Grindelwald is one of the best family experiences in the region and costs very little.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — enjoy a leisurely self-catered breakfast. Take a last short walk through Grindelwald village or along the easy valley path to enjoy the mountain views. Check out of accommodation by 10:00–11:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the train from Grindelwald to Interlaken Ost, then connect to Zurich HB (approx. 2–2.5 hrs). Allow ample time for airport check-in — Zurich Airport is well connected and efficient. Do some last-minute duty-free shopping at the airport for Swiss chocolate and watches if budget allows.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Zurich Airport. Reflect on an incredible week in the Swiss Alps — world-class skiing, breathtaking scenery, and unforgettable family memories, all on a budget-conscious plan.

meals.breakfast: Final self-catered breakfast using remaining supplies (budget CHF 3–5/person)
meals.lunch: Train station or airport food court — grab a sandwich or salad (budget CHF 10–15/person)
meals.dinner: Meal on the plane or at the airport

day_by_day.notes: Keep your Swiss Travel Pass or train tickets handy for the return journey. Zurich Airport has excellent train connections directly from the terminal — no need for a taxi. Arrive at the airport at least 2 hours before your flight. Swiss chocolate from Coop or Migros (bought earlier in the trip) makes the best affordable souvenir — far cheaper than airport shops.

trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight LH arrives at 13:00. Travel time from airport (Zurich or Geneva) to Grindelwald is approximately 2.5–3 hours by train.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at boutique stay in Grindelwald-Wengen by approximately 15:30–16:00. Check in, unpack, and settle in. Take a leisurely stroll through Grindelwald village to get oriented — admire the iconic views of the Eiger North Face, browse local ski rental shops, and pick up lift passes for the week at the Grindelwald Sports or Jungfrau Region ticket office.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a relaxed welcome dinner at the hotel or a nearby village restaurant. Explore the cozy main street of Grindelwald and get an early night to recover from travel.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport — grab a snack at Zurich/Geneva airport before boarding your transfer train.
meals.lunch: Light bite at the train station or on the train — Swiss bakery sandwich or a Migros/Coop grab-and-go meal (~CHF 10–15 per person).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Firestorm or Café 3692 in Grindelwald — hearty Swiss staples like Rösti, Zürcher Geschnetzeltes, or alpine soup. Mid-range dinner ~CHF 30–45 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Purchase your Jungfrau Ski Region lift passes this evening or online in advance to save time on Day 2. Rent ski equipment at a village shop (e.g., Buri Sport or Intersport Grindelwald) — booking ahead is recommended in peak February season. Confirm Jungfraujoch excursion booking for later in the week.

day_by_day.morning: First day on the slopes! Head to the Grindelwald-First ski area — a fantastic beginner-to-intermediate zone ideal for families warming up. Take the Firstbahn gondola up and enjoy wide groomed blue and red runs with stunning Eiger views. Ski from approximately 09:00–12:30.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a mountain lunch break, move over to the Kleine Scheidegg–Männlichen area via the Grindelwald gondola. Explore the long, scenic red runs descending toward Grindelwald Terminal. More experienced skiers in the family can test the Lauberhorn area. Ski until approximately 15:30, then ride back down.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel, freshen up, and enjoy a relaxed family evening. Browse the village or play board games at the hotel lounge.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at the boutique hotel — included or order a continental spread with fresh bread, cheese, cold cuts, and hot drinks (~CHF 15–20 if not included).
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch at Restaurant First or Bergrestaurant Männlichen — try the classic Bergmenü (soup + main) or a Bratwurst with Rösti. ~CHF 20–30 per person on the mountain.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte in Grindelwald — known for its family-friendly atmosphere, wood-fired pizzas, and Swiss classics. ~CHF 25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Dress in warm layers — February temperatures at altitude can drop to -10°C or below. Apply high-SPF sunscreen (50+) as alpine UV is intense even on cloudy days. Helmets are strongly recommended for all family members and available at rental shops.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Snow Tubing and Sledding at Männlichen — a highlight for the whole family! Take the Grindelwald Terminal gondola up to Männlichen (2,229m). Enjoy the dedicated snow tubing and sledding runs with inflatable tubes and traditional sleds. The area offers gentle and more thrilling runs suitable for all ages. Activity runs approximately 09:30–12:00.
day_by_day.afternoon: After tubing, strap back on skis for an afternoon session on the Männlichen plateau. The long, wide blue runs here are perfect for building confidence and enjoying panoramic views of the Jungfrau massif. Alternatively, non-skiing family members can take a guided snowshoe walk along the Männlichen ridge trail (~1.5 hours, easy terrain). Return to Grindelwald by 16:00.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner Experience — gather around a bubbling pot of classic Swiss cheese fondue (Gruyère and Emmental) in a traditional mountain chalet restaurant. A quintessential Swiss evening perfect for families.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fuel up well before a full active day.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch at Männlichen — pack sandwiches and hot drinks in a thermos from the hotel, or grab a quick Wurst and hot chocolate at the Männlichen mountain kiosk (~CHF 10–15 per person).
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner at Restaurant Zum Bären or Chalet Hotel Gletschergarten in Grindelwald — cheese fondue set with bread, pickles, and pearl onions, plus a glass of Swiss wine or hot Ovomaltine for kids. ~CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Snow tubing sessions at Männlichen may require advance booking during peak season — confirm availability the evening before. Sledding equipment is available for rent on-site. The fondue dinner is a memorable cultural experience; consider booking the restaurant table in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' Train Excursion — the unmissable highlight of any Jungfrau Region visit. Depart from Grindelwald Grund station by 08:30 on the historic cogwheel railway via Kleine Scheidegg to Jungfraujoch at 3,454m. Explore the Ice Palace (carved tunnels inside the glacier), the Sphinx Observatory platform with 360° Alpine views, and the Aletsch Glacier — the longest glacier in the Alps. Allow approximately 4–5 hours total for the round trip and exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Grindelwald by approximately 14:00. After the high-altitude excursion, take a gentle afternoon to recover. Visit the Grindelwald Glacier Gorge (Gletscherschlucht) — a stunning 200m-deep ice-carved ravine with illuminated walkways (~45 min walk, CHF 8–10 per adult). A unique and accessible experience for the whole family.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxed evening at the hotel or a casual dinner in the village. Browse local souvenir shops for Swiss chocolates, cheese, and alpine gifts.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast by 07:30 — essential before the Jungfraujoch departure.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Jungfraujoch summit — Crystal Restaurant or the self-service Bollywood Restaurant at the top offers hot meals with surreal glacier views. ~CHF 25–35 per person (slightly elevated prices at altitude).
meals.dinner: Restaurant Mercado or Pizzeria da Salvi in Grindelwald — relaxed mid-range dining with pasta, pizza, and Swiss dishes. ~CHF 25–40 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance — February is peak season and tickets sell out fast. Consider the 'Good Morning Ticket' for a discounted early departure (before 09:00). Dress in extra warm layers — it is extremely cold and windy at 3,454m even in sunshine. Children under 6 ride free on the Jungfrau Railway. Allow time for altitude adjustment — some visitors experience mild headaches at the summit.

day_by_day.morning: Full day of skiing at the Jungfrau Ski Region — today focus on the Wengen side. Take the train from Grindelwald to Wengen (car-free village) and access the Lauberhorn and Männlichen ski areas from the Wengen side. The famous Lauberhorn downhill race course is here — experienced skiers can tackle sections of this legendary FIS World Cup piste. Families with mixed abilities can enjoy the wide intermediate runs around Wengernalp.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing through the afternoon, looping back via Kleine Scheidegg. Try the long top-to-bottom run from Kleine Scheidegg down to Grindelwald Grund (~10km of continuous descent) — one of the great ski runs in the Alps. Return to hotel by 16:30.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski at a local bar or the hotel lounge — enjoy a Glühwein (mulled wine) or hot chocolate. Dinner at a mid-range restaurant in Grindelwald.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — load up with protein and carbohydrates for a big ski day.
meals.lunch: Mountain lunch at Restaurant Kleine Scheidegg or Wengernalp — classic Älplermagronen (Swiss alpine mac and cheese with applesauce) or a hearty soup and bread. ~CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Steinbock in Grindelwald — cozy alpine atmosphere, excellent Raclette and fondue options, good wine list. ~CHF 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The train between Grindelwald and Wengen is covered by the Jungfrau Ski Region lift pass — no extra cost. Wengen is a car-free village, making it particularly peaceful and safe for families. Check snow conditions at Kleine Scheidegg the evening before as wind can close upper lifts.

day_by_day.morning: Cross-Country Skiing and Snowshoeing at Lenk-Simmental — a scenic day trip (~1.5 hrs by car or train) to explore a completely different Alpine landscape. The Lenk-Simmental valley offers 80km of immaculately groomed cross-country (Langlauf) trails through pristine forest and meadows. Beginners can take a short group lesson at the Lenk Nordic Center; experienced skiers can tackle the longer scenic loops. Alternatively, the family can split — some snowshoeing on marked trails while others cross-country ski.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the cross-country or snowshoe experience after lunch, exploring the quieter back-valley trails. This is a wonderful contrast to the busy downhill ski scene — peaceful, scenic, and great exercise. Head back toward Grindelwald by 15:30.
day_by_day.evening: Final special dinner in Grindelwald — treat the family to a memorable last full evening meal at one of the region's top restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — early start for the day trip to Lenk.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Lenkerhof or a traditional Beizli (local inn) in Lenk village — try Bündnerfleisch (air-dried beef), barley soup, or Käseschnitten (Swiss cheese toast). ~CHF 20–30 per person.
meals.dinner: Restaurant Romantik Hotel Schweizerhof in Grindelwald or Aspen Alpine Lifestyle Hotel restaurant — elevated mid-range Swiss cuisine with seasonal alpine ingredients. ~CHF 45–60 per person for a special farewell dinner.

day_by_day.notes: Cross-country ski rentals are available at Lenk Nordic Center (approximately CHF 20–30/day for skis and poles). No lift pass required for cross-country trails — a separate Nordic pass (~CHF 15–20/day) is needed. This activity is excellent for families with younger children or those wanting a rest from downhill skiing. Check train schedules from Grindelwald to Lenk in advance as connections require a change at Spiez.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning ski session — make the most of your last hours on the slopes! Head up to Grindelwald-First one last time for a farewell run with Eiger views. Alternatively, for non-skiers or those resting legs, take a scenic winter walk along the Grindelwald valley floor trail (easy, flat, 3–4km loop through snowy meadows with Wetterhorn and Eiger backdrop). Return to hotel by 11:30 for checkout.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the boutique hotel. Pack up ski rental equipment and return it to the shop. Begin the scenic train journey back to Zurich or Geneva airport — the Bernese Oberland railway through Interlaken and along Lake Thun is stunning even on the return. Allow 2.5–3 hours travel time to the airport.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland — carry home memories of world-class skiing, glacier views, cheese fondue, and alpine adventures.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — enjoy it slowly as a family and soak in the mountain views one last time.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Interlaken during a train connection — Stadthaus Restaurant or a Migros/Coop for a budget-friendly sandwich and Swiss chocolate for the journey. ~CHF 10–20 per person.
meals.dinner: Airport dining at Zurich or Geneva airport, or on the flight home.

day_by_day.notes: Allow extra time for ski equipment return and luggage on departure day — aim to leave Grindelwald no later than 12:00 for a comfortable airport connection. Swiss Federal Railways (SBB) trains run reliably on Sundays. Consider purchasing Swiss chocolate, Gruyère cheese, and alpine souvenirs at Interlaken Ost station or the airport duty-free. Validate all train tickets before boarding.

Begin with a private ski guide for a family orientation run across the Grindelwald-First ski area (2,168m). Enjoy 213km of groomed pistes with runs catering to all skill levels. Warm up on the Blue (easy) runs before progressing to the Red (intermediate) slopes with breathtaking Eiger views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue skiing with your private guide on the Kleine Scheidegg sector, accessing some of the most iconic pistes in the Alps with direct views of the Eiger North Face. After skiing, enjoy a mid-mountain lunch break and then optional snowboarding or freestyle runs for adventurous family members.
day_by_day.evening: Après-ski drinks at the Grindelwald-First or Kleine Scheidegg mountain bar, then return to the hotel for spa recovery — hot tub, sauna, and Alpine wellness treatments. Dinner in the hotel's gourmet restaurant or at a nearby fine dining establishment.

meals.breakfast: Full Swiss breakfast buffet at the boutique hotel — fresh breads, Bircher muesli, cold cuts, cheeses, eggs, fresh juices, and specialty coffee.
meals.lunch: Mountain restaurant lunch at Bergrestaurant Brandegg or Restaurant Grindelwaldblick — fondue, raclette, or hearty Alpine soups with panoramic mountain views. CHF 60–90 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Hotel Belvedere's gourmet restaurant or Romantik Hotel Schweizerhof — multi-course menu featuring seasonal Alpine ingredients. CHF 120–180 per person with wine.

day_by_day.notes: Book a SSCM-certified private ski instructor/guide for the family — highly recommended for maximizing enjoyment and safety. Jungfrau Ski Region pass covers all lifts across First, Männlichen, Kleine Scheidegg, and Mürren-Schilthorn. Ensure children have properly fitted helmets and gear.

day_by_day.morning: Jungfraujoch 'Top of Europe' Train Excursion — depart early from Grindelwald station on the iconic cogwheel railway. Ascend through dramatic Alpine scenery, stopping at Kleine Scheidegg before continuing to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters — the highest railway station in Europe. Explore the Ice Palace, Sphinx Observatory, and take in the awe-inspiring panoramic views of the Aletsch Glacier (UNESCO World Heritage Site).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Jungfraujoch — enjoy snow activities at the summit including a short snowshoe walk on the glacier plateau, dog sledding (seasonal availability), and photo opportunities with the dramatic Jungfrau massif backdrop. Descend back to Grindelwald by mid-afternoon and enjoy some free time for village exploration and luxury Swiss boutique shopping.
day_by_day.evening: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner Experience — gather around a traditional fondue pot in a cozy mountain chalet restaurant. Enjoy classic cheese fondue (Gruyère and Emmental blend), fondue Bourguignonne, and chocolate fondue for dessert, accompanied by Swiss Fendant white wine and schnapps.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast — continental spread with hot options, ensuring an early departure for Jungfraujoch.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Crystal Restaurant or Bollywood Restaurant at Jungfraujoch summit (3,454m) — a truly unique dining experience above the clouds. CHF 50–80 per person.
meals.dinner: Swiss Alpine Fondue Dinner at Chalet-Restaurant Onkel Tom's Hütte or Restaurant Firehut, Grindelwald — full fondue experience with wine pairings. CHF 80–120 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Jungfraujoch train tickets well in advance — this is one of Switzerland's most popular excursions. Departure from Grindelwald recommended by 08:30 to beat crowds. Bring sunglasses (UV protection critical at altitude), warm layers, and lip balm. Children under 16 receive discounted rail fares. Allow 5–6 hours total for the excursion.

day_by_day.morning: Glacier Snow Tubing and Sledding at Männlichen — take the Grindelwald-Männlichen gondola (one of the world's longest gondola rides at 6.2km) up to Männlichen (2,230m). Enjoy a thrilling family-friendly morning of snow tubing on inflatable tubes and traditional wooden sledding on dedicated runs. This is a perfect activity for all ages and requires no skiing experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: After snow tubing, strap on snowshoes for a guided family snowshoeing tour along the scenic Männlichen ridge with panoramic views of the Jungfrau, Mönch, and Eiger. Return to the valley by gondola and spend the afternoon at the hotel's luxury spa — indoor pool, steam room, and family relaxation area. Optional: book individual Alpine massage treatments.
day_by_day.evening: Private fondue or raclette dinner experience arranged in-room or in a private chalet dining setting — hotel concierge can arrange an exclusive private chef experience with a local culinary expert serving traditional Swiss dishes in an intimate setting.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely full hotel breakfast buffet — take time to enjoy the morning before heading to Männlichen.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Restaurant Männlichen at the summit — Alpine cuisine with spectacular Grindelwald valley views. Try the Älplermagronen (Alpine macaroni) or hearty mountain soup. CHF 50–70 per person.
meals.dinner: Private in-suite or chalet dining experience arranged by hotel concierge — 3-course Swiss menu with raclette station, curated wine selection, and artisan Swiss chocolate dessert. CHF 200–300 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Grindelwald-Männlichen gondola is family-friendly and stroller/equipment accessible. Snow tubing at Männlichen is weather-dependent — confirm with hotel concierge the morning of. Book spa treatments 24–48 hours in advance. Private chef dinner requires at least 48 hours' notice through the hotel concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Second premium ski day at Jungfrau Ski Region — focus on the Wengen and Lauberhorn sector, accessible via the Wengernalp railway from Grindelwald. Ski the famous Lauberhorn downhill race course (venue of the annual World Cup race) with your private guide. Advanced family members can tackle the legendary 4.48km Lauberhorn descent while beginners enjoy the gentler Wengen slopes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Ski over to Mürren via Kleine Scheidegg and Allmendhubel — explore the car-free village of Mürren and ski the Schilthorn sector with views made famous by the James Bond film 'On Her Majesty's Secret Service.' Visit the revolving Piz Gloria restaurant at the Schilthorn summit (2,970m) for a panoramic afternoon break. Return to Grindelwald via train and gondola.
day_by_day.evening: Upscale après-ski and dinner at one of Grindelwald's finest establishments. Recommended: The Aspen Restaurant at Grand Hotel Regina — contemporary Alpine cuisine featuring seasonal truffle dishes, prime Swiss beef, and an extensive wine cellar with over 400 labels.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast — fuel up for a full day of skiing.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the iconic Piz Gloria revolving restaurant, Schilthorn (2,970m) — enjoy the Bond-themed menu or Alpine classics while the restaurant slowly rotates 360° offering unparalleled mountain views. CHF 60–90 per person.
meals.dinner: Fine dining at The Aspen Restaurant, Grand Hotel Regina, Grindelwald — 5-course tasting menu with wine pairing. CHF 180–250 per person. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Wengen sector is only accessible by train (no cars in Wengen) — a uniquely charming experience. The Lauberhorn run is best skied with a guide for safety and route knowledge. Mürren-Schilthorn sector requires additional travel via cable car from Lauterbrunnen — allow extra time. Book Piz Gloria lunch reservation in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Cross-Country Skiing and Snowshoeing at Lenk-Simmental — enjoy a premium day trip (approximately 1.5 hours by private transfer) to Lenk-Simmental, offering 80km of immaculately groomed cross-country ski trails and scenic snowshoe paths through pristine Alpine forests. Hire local expert guides for a family cross-country skiing lesson and exploration of the Simmental valley's stunning winter landscape.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue exploring Lenk-Simmental's snowshoe trails through the Iffigenalp nature reserve — a magical winter wonderland with frozen waterfalls and untouched Alpine scenery. Enjoy a warming break at a traditional Beizli (Alpine farmhouse inn) before the private transfer returns you to Grindelwald by late afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relaxing final full evening — enjoy the hotel spa, then a celebratory farewell dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant or a top Grindelwald establishment. Splurge on a premium Swiss wine from the Valais region and indulge in a decadent dessert of Vermicelles (chestnut purée) or Swiss chocolate soufflé.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast before departure for Lenk-Simmental.
meals.lunch: Traditional lunch at a Lenk-Simmental farmhouse restaurant — homemade Berner Platte (assorted meats and sauerkraut), Alpine cheese board, and mulled wine. CHF 50–70 per person.
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at Restaurant Alte Post, Grindelwald, or hotel signature dining — premium 6-course tasting menu featuring Valais lamb, Alpine herbs, and artisan Swiss cheese selection with sommelier-guided wine pairing. CHF 200–280 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Private transfer to Lenk-Simmental is recommended over public transport for comfort and flexibility — arrange through hotel concierge. Cross-country ski equipment rental is available in Lenk village. This day offers a wonderful contrast to downhill skiing — ideal for family members seeking a gentler, more scenic Alpine experience. Snowshoe trails are suitable for children aged 6 and above.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning leisure — enjoy a slow, indulgent hotel breakfast with panoramic Alpine views. Take a final scenic walk through Grindelwald village, visit the local artisan shops for premium Swiss souvenirs (Lindt chocolates, Swiss watches, handcrafted wooden items, local cheese and wine). Optional: one last short ski run or gondola ride to Grindelwald-First for a farewell view of the Eiger.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of the boutique hotel after a final spa visit or relaxation session. Private luxury transfer departs for Zurich or Geneva airport — approximately 2.5–3 hours. Enjoy the scenic Swiss countryside during the transfer.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Switzerland. If flight is late evening, enjoy a premium airport lounge experience at Zurich (SWISS First Class Lounge or Aspire Lounge) or Geneva (No. 1 Traveller Lounge) with fine dining, spa facilities, and premium beverages before boarding.

meals.breakfast: Extended luxury farewell breakfast at the hotel — full spread with made-to-order eggs, smoked salmon, artisan pastries, Swiss cheeses, and specialty coffees. Savor every last bite with mountain views.
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch in Grindelwald village before departure — café or bistro with Swiss-style sandwiches, soups, and pastries. CHF 30–50 per person. Alternatively, a packed luxury picnic hamper arranged by the hotel for the transfer journey.
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or on-board premium cabin meal. Alternatively, if time permits before a late flight, dinner at a Zurich city restaurant near the airport — Restaurant Clouds at Prime Tower (Zurich) offers stunning city views and contemporary Swiss cuisine.

day_by_day.notes: Arrange hotel late checkout (if available) to maximize your final morning without rushing. Confirm private transfer timing with hotel concierge the evening before. Allow extra time at the airport for Swiss customs and duty-free shopping — Switzerland has excellent duty-free selections including Toblerone, Lindt, Swiss Army knives, and luxury watches. Ensure ski equipment rentals are returned before departure.
